question: A Lambda function holds sensitive database credentials. What is the most secure pattern for storing and retrieving them at runtime?
options: A. Store credentials in AWS Secrets Manager and have the function retrieve them at runtime; grant the function's role secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
B. Hard-code credentials in the function source code
C. Pass credentials as plain-text Lambda environment variables
D. Embed them in an S3 file with a public read ACL
correct: A. Store credentials in AWS Secrets Manager and have the function retrieve them at runtime; grant the function's role secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
explanation: Secrets Manager encrypts secrets with KMS, supports automatic rotation, and exposes versioned secrets to authorized principals via IAM. Hard-coding or plain-text env vars expose secrets to anyone who can view the code or configuration.

question: A web application running on EC2 must access S3 and DynamoDB. Which authentication pattern is recommended?
options: A. Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance via an instance profile; the SDK picks up temporary credentials from IMDS automatically
B. Store an IAM user's access keys in a config file on disk
C. Use the AWS account root user's access keys
D. Pass keys to the application as command-line arguments
correct: A. Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance via an instance profile; the SDK picks up temporary credentials from IMDS automatically
explanation: Instance roles deliver short-lived credentials that the SDK retrieves transparently. No long-lived keys live on disk, and credentials rotate automatically.

question: A team wants only allow-listed corporate IP ranges to reach the management console of an internal web app behind an ALB. Which AWS service applies the IP filter at the edge?
options: A. AWS WAF (with an IP set rule) attached to the ALB
B. Amazon GuardDuty
C. AWS Trusted Advisor
D. AWS Certificate Manager
correct: A. AWS WAF (with an IP set rule) attached to the ALB
explanation: AWS WAF integrates with CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, and App Runner to enforce L7 rules including IP-set allow/deny lists.

question: A stateless web tier on EC2 must survive the loss of a single Availability Zone with no manual intervention. Which architecture meets this?
options: A. Auto Scaling group across at least two AZs behind an Application Load Balancer with health checks
B. Single large EC2 instance pinned to one AZ
C. Many EC2 instances in one AZ behind a Classic Load Balancer
D. EC2 instance hibernation with cold start
correct: A. Auto Scaling group across at least two AZs behind an Application Load Balancer with health checks
explanation: Spreading capacity across AZs plus ALB health checks plus Auto Scaling self-healing produces zone-redundant, self-healing compute.

question: Which Amazon RDS feature provides synchronous AZ-redundant storage and automatic failover for a relational workload?
options: A. Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment
B. Read replicas in the same AZ
C. Daily manual snapshots
D. Aurora Backtrack
correct: A. Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment
explanation: Multi-AZ replicates data synchronously to a standby in another AZ; on failure RDS fails over (60–120 s) and CNAME updates redirect clients. Read replicas address read scale, not HA; backups are recovery, not HA.

question: A workload must continue serving traffic if an entire AWS Region fails. Which design fits an active-active strategy?
options: A. Deploy active stacks in two Regions, replicate data with Aurora Global Database, and route users with Route 53 latency-based routing or AWS Global Accelerator
B. Run in a single Region with Multi-AZ
C. Take cross-Region S3 backups only
D. Use only CloudFront edge caching
correct: A. Deploy active stacks in two Regions, replicate data with Aurora Global Database, and route users with Route 53 latency-based routing or AWS Global Accelerator
explanation: Multi-Region active-active spreads live traffic across Regions; Aurora Global Database, DynamoDB Global Tables, and S3 CRR keep data in sync. Single-Region designs do not survive Region failure.

question: To recover an Amazon S3 object that a developer accidentally overwrote, which feature is required on the bucket?
options: A. S3 Versioning enabled on the bucket
B. S3 Intelligent-Tiering
C. S3 Transfer Acceleration
D. S3 Replication Time Control
correct: A. S3 Versioning enabled on the bucket
explanation: With versioning enabled, every PUT creates a new version and the previous version is retained. Deletes are non-destructive (delete markers) and the prior object version can be restored.

question: A read-heavy web application is bottlenecked on its PostgreSQL database. Which option offloads reads with the smallest application change?
options: A. Create one or more Amazon RDS read replicas and route read traffic to the replica endpoint(s)
B. Increase the instance size again and again forever
C. Move the database to S3
D. Replace PostgreSQL with DynamoDB
correct: A. Create one or more Amazon RDS read replicas and route read traffic to the replica endpoint(s)
explanation: Read replicas let you scale read capacity horizontally and require only routing reads to the replica endpoint. Vertical scaling has limits; replacing the engine is a major rewrite.

question: An image-processing job runs in parallel on thousands of independent files. Which compute option is most cost-effective?
options: A. Spot Instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group (or Spot capacity on AWS Batch/ECS/EKS)
B. On-Demand m6i.32xlarge running 24/7
C. Dedicated Hosts
D. One Lambda function per file with provisioned concurrency
correct: A. Spot Instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group (or Spot capacity on AWS Batch/ECS/EKS)
explanation: Spot offers up to ~90% off On-Demand and is ideal for fault-tolerant, parallel batch workloads where workers can be interrupted and replaced.

question: A global REST API needs the lowest possible client latency from any continent. Which service is purpose-built?
options: A. Amazon CloudFront in front of a regional API Gateway (or AWS Global Accelerator)
B. A single API Gateway in one Region with no caching
C. EC2 instances in one Region behind an NLB
D. Static S3 hosting
correct: A. Amazon CloudFront in front of a regional API Gateway (or AWS Global Accelerator)
explanation: CloudFront terminates TLS and caches at edge locations close to users; Global Accelerator routes traffic over the AWS backbone to the nearest healthy Regional endpoint.

question: A real-time dashboard requires sub-millisecond key-value reads at extreme scale. Which AWS service is best suited?
options: A. Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), or Amazon ElastiCache for Redis
B. Amazon Athena
C. Amazon Redshift
D. Amazon RDS for MySQL
correct: A. Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), or Amazon ElastiCache for Redis
explanation: DAX is a write-through in-memory cache in front of DynamoDB, and ElastiCache for Redis serves cached data at sub-millisecond latency. Athena, Redshift, and RDS are not designed for sub-millisecond reads at that scale.

question: A company runs a steady-state production workload on the same EC2 instance family 24/7 for the next 3 years. What is the most cost-effective purchase option?
options: A. A 3-year Compute Savings Plan (or Standard Reserved Instances) with All Upfront payment
B. On-Demand pricing
C. Spot Instances
D. Lightsail bundle
correct: A. A 3-year Compute Savings Plan (or Standard Reserved Instances) with All Upfront payment
explanation: 3-year commitments with All Upfront payment offer the deepest discount (up to ~72%). Compute Savings Plans also flex across families, sizes, OS, and Region.

question: Which feature automatically tiers Amazon S3 objects between frequent, infrequent, and archive access classes based on observed usage?
options: A. S3 Intelligent-Tiering
B. S3 Standard-IA
C. S3 Glacier Deep Archive
D. S3 One Zone-IA
correct: A. S3 Intelligent-Tiering
explanation: Intelligent-Tiering monitors access per object and moves objects between tiers automatically, with no retrieval fees, for a small monitoring fee per object.

question: A nightly batch job reads 5 TB of data, runs for 30 minutes, and then the cluster is no longer needed. Which compute option minimizes idle cost?
options: A. Spot Instances in a transient cluster (e.g., EMR on EC2 Spot, AWS Batch, or terminating ASG)
B. A 3-year Reserved Instance
C. Dedicated Host
D. Lightsail
correct: A. Spot Instances in a transient cluster (e.g., EMR on EC2 Spot, AWS Batch, or terminating ASG)
explanation: Short-lived, fault-tolerant jobs map naturally to Spot. RIs and Dedicated Hosts assume long-term steady-state use.

question: Which AWS service produces forecasts of upcoming AWS spend based on historical usage?
options: A. AWS Cost Explorer (forecast view)
B. AWS Pricing Calculator
C. AWS Trusted Advisor
D. Amazon CloudWatch metrics
correct: A. AWS Cost Explorer (forecast view)
explanation: Cost Explorer can project future spend based on historical patterns. The Pricing Calculator estimates planned (not yet deployed) workloads, Trusted Advisor flags savings, and CloudWatch tracks performance metrics.

question: To privately connect an Amazon VPC to Amazon S3 without traversing the public internet, which feature should be used?
options: A. An S3 Gateway VPC endpoint (or S3 Interface endpoint via PrivateLink)
B. NAT Gateway
C. Internet Gateway
D. VPC peering between two VPCs
correct: A. An S3 Gateway VPC endpoint (or S3 Interface endpoint via PrivateLink)
explanation: A Gateway endpoint targets S3/DynamoDB via route table entries with no extra cost. Interface endpoints (PrivateLink) provide ENI-based connectivity with DNS resolution to private IPs.

question: Two VPCs in different AWS accounts need to communicate using private IPs. Which is the simplest construct?
options: A. VPC peering
B. A NAT Gateway in each VPC
C. An Internet Gateway
D. AWS Direct Connect
correct: A. VPC peering
explanation: VPC peering is a non-transitive private connection between two VPCs (same or different accounts/Regions). Transit Gateway is preferred when many VPCs must mesh.

question: A company has many VPCs and needs them all to share private connectivity through a hub. Which AWS service simplifies this?
options: A. AWS Transit Gateway
B. Many pair-wise VPC peerings
C. A NAT Gateway per VPC
D. AWS Storage Gateway
correct: A. AWS Transit Gateway
explanation: Transit Gateway acts as a regional hub for VPCs, on-premises VPN/Direct Connect, and other networks, avoiding the n² mesh of pair-wise peering.

question: Which AWS service is a managed POSIX file system that many EC2 instances can mount concurrently across AZs?
options: A. Amazon Elastic File System (EFS)
B. Amazon EBS
C. Amazon S3
D. Instance store
correct: A. Amazon Elastic File System (EFS)
explanation: EFS exposes NFSv4 to many EC2 instances simultaneously across multiple AZs; EBS is single-instance block storage; S3 is object; instance store is ephemeral.

question: Which Amazon FSx variant should be chosen for high-performance Windows file shares (SMB) shared across multiple workloads?
options: A. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
B. Amazon FSx for Lustre
C. Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP (also valid for SMB but not Windows-native)
D. Amazon FSx for OpenZFS
correct: A. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
explanation: FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed Windows-native SMB shares with AD integration. Lustre is for HPC, ONTAP and OpenZFS offer different protocol blends.

question: A team needs durable storage for cold compliance archives that must be retrievable within 12 hours and kept for 10+ years at the lowest cost. Which storage class fits?
options: A. Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive
B. Amazon S3 Standard
C. Amazon EBS gp3
D. Instance store
correct: A. Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive
explanation: Deep Archive is the cheapest S3 storage class, intended for long-term archives accessed only rarely with retrieval times up to 12 hours.

question: A producer service needs to send messages to multiple, independent downstream consumers. Which pub/sub-style service is appropriate?
options: A. Amazon SNS (fan-out to multiple subscribers, including SQS queues and Lambda)
B. Amazon SQS standard queue (one logical consumer group)
C. Amazon SES
D. AWS Storage Gateway
correct: A. Amazon SNS (fan-out to multiple subscribers, including SQS queues and Lambda)
explanation: SNS topics fan out one message to many subscribers (SQS, Lambda, HTTPS, email, mobile push). SQS is point-to-point; SES is email; Storage Gateway is hybrid storage.

question: A long-running orchestration must coordinate multiple Lambda functions with retries, branching, and error handling. Which service is built for this?
options: A. AWS Step Functions
B. Amazon SQS
C. Amazon SNS
D. AWS Batch
correct: A. AWS Step Functions
explanation: Step Functions expresses workflows as state machines (standard or express) with built-in retry/catch, parallel, choice, and wait states — ideal for multi-step orchestration.

question: A REST API needs to authenticate millions of mobile users with sign-up, sign-in, and social federation. Which AWS service handles user identity for the app?
options: A. Amazon Cognito user pools (with federation to social/SAML IdPs as needed)
B. AWS IAM users created per end-user
C. AWS Directory Service for Microsoft AD
D. AWS Single Sign-On (for workforce identity)
correct: A. Amazon Cognito user pools (with federation to social/SAML IdPs as needed)
explanation: Cognito user pools manage end-user identity and tokens for apps and APIs. IAM is for AWS access, not end users; Directory Service runs AD; IAM Identity Center is for workforce SSO into AWS.

question: A company wants new EC2 instances to apply a baseline configuration (install agents, configure logs) at first boot. Which mechanism is the AWS-native default?
options: A. EC2 user data scripts (with cloud-init), optionally combined with AWS Systems Manager State Manager for ongoing enforcement
B. SSH into each new instance manually
C. AWS Config rules
D. Hard-code into the Auto Scaling group
correct: A. EC2 user data scripts (with cloud-init), optionally combined with AWS Systems Manager State Manager for ongoing enforcement
explanation: User data runs on first boot to bootstrap an instance; combined with SSM State Manager (or Ansible/Chef/Puppet), it keeps the instance configured over time.

question: A team needs to securely share an Amazon RDS snapshot with another AWS account for testing. What is the recommended approach?
options: A. Modify the snapshot's permissions to share it with the target AWS account ID (use a custom KMS key for encrypted snapshots and share the key)
B. Make the snapshot public
C. Email a database dump file
D. Open the source DB security group to the target account VPC
correct: A. Modify the snapshot's permissions to share it with the target AWS account ID (use a custom KMS key for encrypted snapshots and share the key)
explanation: RDS snapshots support cross-account sharing via permissions. Encrypted snapshots additionally require the target account to have permission on the customer-managed KMS key (not the default AWS-managed key).

question: A team needs to enforce that every EBS volume created across the organization is encrypted by default. What is the simplest way?
options: A. Enable EBS encryption by default in each Region (account-level setting); optionally enforce with an SCP
B. Email developers a reminder
C. Run a daily Lambda that re-creates unencrypted volumes
D. Disable EBS in the account
correct: A. Enable EBS encryption by default in each Region (account-level setting); optionally enforce with an SCP
explanation: EBS encryption by default is a one-click per-Region account setting. An SCP can additionally deny `ec2:CreateVolume` requests that lack encryption to enforce organization-wide.

question: An on-premises application generates 10 TB of files per day that must be replicated to Amazon S3 with bandwidth limits to avoid saturating the office link. Which AWS service is purpose-built?
options: A. AWS DataSync (with bandwidth throttling)
B. AWS Snowball Edge for a one-time bulk move
C. S3 Transfer Acceleration for clients
D. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
correct: A. AWS DataSync (with bandwidth throttling)
explanation: DataSync is a managed online data-transfer service that moves files into AWS storage at high speed with bandwidth limits, scheduling, and verification. Snowball is offline; Transfer Acceleration is for individual uploads.

question: Which AWS feature lets you grant a Lambda function in account A read-only access to a DynamoDB table in account B?
options: A. Create an IAM role in account B with the required DynamoDB permissions and a trust policy allowing the Lambda execution role in account A to assume it
B. Share the access keys of an IAM user in account B with the function
C. Make the DynamoDB table public
D. Use the AWS root user of account B
correct: A. Create an IAM role in account B with the required DynamoDB permissions and a trust policy allowing the Lambda execution role in account A to assume it
explanation: Cross-account access uses sts:AssumeRole — the source principal assumes a role in the target account that has the necessary permissions. Sharing long-lived credentials or making data public is unsafe.

question: Which managed AWS service is the simplest choice for hosting a containerized application without managing any EC2 hosts?
options: A. Amazon ECS (or EKS) on AWS Fargate
B. Self-managed Kubernetes on EC2
C. Lightsail Linux instance
D. EC2 Spot fleet without orchestration
correct: A. Amazon ECS (or EKS) on AWS Fargate
explanation: Fargate is the serverless capacity for ECS and EKS — AWS provisions and manages the compute for you; the customer only defines the task or pod.
